Done. The final solution.py is in place and verified.

Summary: Implemented Kimi Delta Attention chunk-forward from scratch as two custom Triton kernels for SM120 — a fully-parallel per-chunk prep kernel (in-chunk g cumsum, decay-scaled k·kᵀ, (I+M)⁻¹ via Neumann doubling, w/u/Aqk/z/t2/kg2) plus a sequential inter-chunk kernel with the recurrent state tile resident in registers (w/z stacked into one dot, V-tiling for parallelism, padded-kg2 state update), with a known-good fallback kernel and a cross-call buffer cache. Validated the math end-to-end in numpy against reference.py before porting; remote runs show `status: correct` on all 4 shapes × 3 seeds × scale-stress × property-stress (the structured long-memory case required fp32-ieee inversion dots — tf32 breaks the alternating series' cancellation). Best measured config: peak_fraction 0.0155 (prep ≈114µs, seq ≈52µs at B=2,T=1024,H=8); final file reverts the one regression found (prep num_warps=16) back to the proven run-5 setup plus the validated buffer cache. Practice runs are exhausted; solution.py compiles clean with no forbidden imports/strings.
